title: Canonical completed scalar comparison data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E,L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, an algebra embedding $\iota:E\to L$, and a scheme $Y$. Use the residue-normalized completed coefficient map $c:R_E\to R_L$ and its ordinary sheafified scalar extension [def-weil-completed-integral-scalar-data] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $T$ be its ordinary extension functor on sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $\mathbf LT$ its derived extension [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $\varepsilon_P:\mathbf LT(QP)\to Q(TP)$ its universal computation counit on a K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Let $S$ be the completed integral scalar extension, formed from the quotient extension tower [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] using its derived inverse limit [def-weil-derived-limit]. Define $\chi:\mathbf LT\to S$ to be the uniquely normalized natural transformation whose restriction to good representatives, followed by the canonical comparison $S(QP)\simeq S_{\mathrm{good}}(P)$, is $\varepsilon_P$ followed by $Q$ of the strict quotient-Roos comparison. The latter sends a tensor $s\otimes x$ to its sequence of finite quotient tensors in the unshifted product coordinate and zero in the shifted coordinate. Thus $\chi$ is the published unique derived descent of that strict comparison; no invertibility assertion is part of this definition. Coefficient and scheme universes are independent.
